briefdescription.para: Checks a condition and, if false, stops the test case.

detaileddescription.para: The failure is reported and counted as for expect(); then, when exceptions are enabled, the rest of the test case body is skipped, and the run continues with the next test case, as ASSERT_* in GoogleTest, REQUIRE() in Catch2 and doctest, and BOOST_REQUIRE() in Boost.Test do. Without exceptions, the test execution is aborted with runner::abort().

The test case is stopped by throwing a private exception, at the end of the statement, after the optional message was appended. It is not derived from std::exception; a catch (...) in the test case body must rethrow it, and the body must not be noexcept.

Expr_T
The type of the custom expression.
Constraints
Enabled only if Expr_T is a framework expression type or is contextually convertible to bool, including by an explicit operator bool (enforced via a C++20 requires clause, with extension::checkable).
expr
Logical expression to evaluate.
sl
Optional source location, defaulting to the current line.
result
The check result, a temporary created by the caller as the default argument, which the applications do not pass; it is destroyed at the end of the statement.
A reference to the check result, to which optional messages can be appended with operator<<; the check is reported when it is destroyed, at the end of the statement, so the result cannot be kept in a variable.
Initialises the detail::check_result received as the last argument, a temporary created by the caller, with the kind detail::check_kind::requirement, and returns a reference to it. The check result evaluates the condition when initialised, records a pass or fail when it is destroyed, and, if the condition is false, stops the test case by throwing detail::failed_requirement (caught by test_case::run()), or, without exceptions, aborts the test execution.

Stops the compilation with the message of the static_assert, which states what require() takes. The condition of the static_assert depends on the type, so it is evaluated only when the function is selected.
Deprecated; the check is the same as that of require(), for the arguments that are always true.

briefdescription.para: Requirements are checks that stop the test case when they fail.

detaileddescription.para: When a precondition of the following checks does not hold, the test case cannot continue meaningfully. A failed requirement is reported and counted like a failed expectation, and then the rest of the test case body is skipped; the run continues with the next test case.

This is the behaviour of the fatal assertions of most C++ test frameworks (ASSERT_* in GoogleTest, REQUIRE() in Catch2 and doctest, BOOST_REQUIRE() in Boost.Test). The test case is stopped with an exception; without exceptions, it cannot be stopped alone, so the results of the test case are reported, ending with the failed requirement (followed, with the TAP reporter, by a Bail out! line), and the whole test execution is aborted with runner::abort(), as Catch2 does; the remaining test cases do not run, and no totals are written.
